doc.title: Sheila Jordan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Lyrics for Dannie Richmond's Soft Seas
summary: At Cameron's urging she writes words for Dannie Richmond's calypso Soft Seas, picturing him going home to be buried.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And then he got me to write some lyrics to, um, Dannie Richmond‟s… Brown, C.: To a tune by Dannie called Soft Seas.
Called Soft Seas. Brown, C.: The calypso that Dannie wrote.
And I wrote and, and… Brown, C.: And she wrote some beautiful lyrics to commemorate Dannie.
It has like an under thing. Yeah. Brown, C.: Yeah.

But you, you know, you could just take it going home again. But in my lyrics, what I saw when Cameron told me to think about writing some lyrics, I saw Dannie going back to his homeland to be buried or to, you know, bid his farewell to his loved ones. That‟s what I felt. Soft seas are taking me home again, back to the place where I left my next of kin. Your love has carried me through. No more will I roam. Soft seas take me back home to you. So, you know… So that just came like that. Boom. But at his encouragement. „Cause had he not said anything, I wouldn‟t have done it. Brown, C.: Well, that all, but see that came out of this project that I was working on.
